editorial:
Imagine a world where a hungry coyote decides that being smart isn't enough, so he brings in a giant supercomputer to do the thinking for him. You get to watch Wile E. Coyote try to outsmart the legendary Bugs Bunny using a Univac Electronic Brain, which is basically the 1950s version of a high-tech AI. The whole vibe is classic slapstick gold. It is a funny battle of wits where the machine makes a perfect plan, but the chaotic nature of Bugs Bunny turns everything into a giant mess. It is a lighthearted ride that feels like a timeless game of cat and mouse, or in this case, coyote and rabbit.

What really stands out is how the pacing never slows down. The timing of the gags is perfect, and seeing the huge machine fail in such silly ways is the best part. While it is a short cartoon, the animation holds up great. If you want the best experience, you should try to find a restored version on a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection, or just stream it in high definition on a service like Prime Video. It is a great pick for families or anyone who needs a quick laugh. You will love how the high-tech logic fails against simple luck.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when the supercomputer comes up with a final, foolproof plan to catch Bugs. However, the machine is too rigid for its own good. In the end, the plan backfires completely. The computer ends up causing its own destruction, leaving Wile E. Coyote defeated once again. Bugs Bunny wins without even trying, proving that no matter how much math or technology you use, you cannot beat a clever rabbit.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Looney Tunes and slapstick humor.
